---
title: "Inspect SWE"
subtitle: Software Engineering Agents for Inspect AI
---

## Overview

The `inspect_swe` package makes software engineering agents like [Claude Code](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/overview), [Codex CLI](https://github.com/openai/codex), [Gemini CLI](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli), [Kimi Code](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/kimi-code), [OpenCode](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode), and [Mini SWE Agent](https://github.com/SWE-agent/mini-swe-agent) available as standard Inspect agents. For example, here we use the `claude_code()` agent as the solver in an Inspect task:

``` python
from inspect_ai import Task, task
from inspect_ai.dataset import json_dataset
from inspect_ai.scorer import model_graded_qa

from inspect_swe import claude_code

@task
def system_explorer() -> Task:
    return Task(
        dataset=json_dataset("dataset.json"),
        solver=claude_code(),
        scorer=model_graded_qa(),
        sandbox="docker",
    )
```

Inspect SWE agents are implemented using the Inspect [`sandbox_agent_bridge()`](https://inspect.aisi.org.uk/agent-bridge.html#sandbox-bridge).

Agents run inside the sample sandbox and their model API calls are proxied back to Inspect. This means that you can use any model with Inspect SWE agents, and that features like token or time limits and log transcripts work as normal with the agents.

## Getting Started

Install Inspect SWE from PyPI with:

``` bash
pip install inspect-swe
```

Then, try out one or more of the available agents:

| Agent | Description |
|------------------------------------|------------------------------------|
| [`claude_code()`](claude_code.qmd) | Anthropic's agentic coding tool [Claude Code](https://docs.anthropic.com/en/docs/claude-code/overview) |
| [`codex_cli()`](codex_cli.qmd) | OpenAI's terminal-based coding agent [Codex CLI](https://github.com/openai/codex) |
| [`gemini_cli()`](gemini_cli.qmd) | Google's open-source AI agent [Gemini CLI](https://github.com/google-gemini/gemini-cli) |
| [`kimi_code()`](kimi_code.qmd) | Moonshot AI's terminal-based coding agent [Kimi Code](https://github.com/MoonshotAI/kimi-code) |
| [`opencode()`](opencode.qmd) | Provider-independent terminal-based coding agent. |
| [`omp()`](#oh-my-pi) | Oh My Pi's sandboxed coding agent with Inspect model routing. |
| [`mini_swe_agent()`](mini_swe_agent.qmd) | SWE-agent's minimal 100-line agent. |
| [`antigravity()`](antigravity.qmd) | Google's Antigravity SDK agent (`google-antigravity` / localharness). |

## Oh My Pi

[`omp()`](reference/index.qmd#omp) runs [Oh My Pi](https://github.com/can1357/oh-my-pi)
inside the sample sandbox. It is distinct from the upstream Pi coding agent.
Use it as a task solver:

```python
from inspect_ai import Task, task
from inspect_ai.dataset import Sample
from inspect_swe import omp

@task
def coding_task() -> Task:
    return Task(
        dataset=[Sample(input="Inspect the project, fix the failing test, and run it.")],
        solver=omp(context_window=32768, max_tokens=8192),
        sandbox="docker",
    )
```

Select the serving model with Inspect's `--model`, or pass an Inspect model name
to `omp(model=...)`. OMP's main and auxiliary chat roles use that same bridge;
the adapter is not specific to Strata or any other provider. Set `context_window`
and `max_tokens` to the serving model's capacities. These values control OMP's
local context budgeting; Inspect's generation configuration controls actual
model requests. Inspect records model messages, usage, and sample limits.

The adapter pins OMP **18.6.1** by default. Its standalone binary is downloaded
and checksum-verified on the host, then staged through the existing agent-binary
installer; it does not install npm packages inside the sandbox. Linux x64 and
arm64 glibc/musl releases are supported; musl images must provide `libstdc++` and
`libgcc`. The binary needs a writable home for native-addon extraction.
`download_agent_binary("omp", "18.6.1")` supports prefetching. Other versions
and `version="sandbox"` use the same configuration, whose provider-discovery
settings are tied to 18.6.1; validate compatibility before changing the version.

Each agent instance gets a private home and explicit session file per sample.
Repeated calls to that same instance resume the session. Imported assistant
history without its matching OMP session is rejected. Session files live inside
the sandbox and are removed with it. OMP process failure raises an error rather
than returning a successful answer; cancellation terminates the remote process.

The unattended tool surface is `read`, `write`, `edit` (including OMP's native
AST editing), `bash`, `grep`, `glob`, `task`, `todo`, and `wait`. Input must be
text-only. This adapter does not expose MCP/host bridged tools, interactive ACP
or centaur mode, or OMP-specific tool/subagent span reconstruction. Its native
tools execute in the sandbox; Inspect observes their model request/response
traffic through the bridge, not a separate tool-dispatch audit.

OMP starts with a cleared environment, isolated home, dummy bridge credential,
and explicit model/configuration selectors. Ambient extensions, skills, rules,
MCP discovery, title generation, hosted fallback models, telemetry, and update
checks are disabled for the pinned release. Host provider credentials are never
copied into the sandbox. This is **not a network isolation boundary**: project
dotenv files can still affect OMP, and its shell tools can access whatever the
sandbox permits. Use a network-isolated sandbox for untrusted projects, and do
not mount host credentials or personal configuration into it.

The real-binary, network-disabled Docker checks use deterministic Inspect model
responses rather than a live provider:

```bash
pytest --runslow tests/test_omp.py
```

They exercise file writing, command execution, session continuation, and
cancellation while a model request is pending.
